richText: A dependency is another object that a class uses.
Dependency injection means supplying that object to the class instead of making the class create it.
For constructor injection, Spring finds a matching bean and passes it to the constructor.
A class with one constructor does not need @Autowired on that constructor.

example.title: Inject GreetingService into a controller
description: Use the GreetingService bean from the beans lesson. Add Spring Web and place the controller in the scanned package tree.
explanation: Spring creates the controller and supplies the GreetingService bean.
The constructor stores the dependency in a final field.
GET /greeting calls greeting(), which calls the service.

richText: Constructor injection makes required dependencies explicit. A caller can also supply them when creating the object without Spring.
Setter injection supplies a dependency through a method after construction. It can represent an optional dependency.
Field injection writes directly to an annotated field after construction. That field is unavailable inside the constructor.
Using new to construct a class yourself does not ask Spring to inject its fields.
If Spring cannot find a required dependency, creating the consuming bean fails. Check registration and scanning.
If several beans match the requested type, use @Qualifier to name the intended bean or @Primary to designate the default candidate.
@Autowired can mark a constructor when Spring needs to know which constructor to use.
Two beans whose constructors require each other create a circular dependency. Constructor injection cannot resolve that cycle.
